records.question: Was there a seasonal difference in coral disease prevalence between Winter 2004 and Summer 2005 on Tutuila?
records.ground_truth_answer: No — there were no seasonal differences; average coral disease prevalence was 0.21% (SE±0.08) in Winter 2004 and 0.15% (SE±0.05) in Summer 2005 (Wilcoxon signed rank, n=14, p=0.29).
ground_truth_chunks: There were no seasonal differences found in coral disease prevalence or CLOD abundance. Average coral disease prevalence was 0.21% (SE±0.08) in Winter 2004 as compared to 0.15% (SE±0.05) in Summer 2005 (Wilcoxon signed rank, n=14, p=0.29).
CLOD levels were 0.039 (SE±0.03) CLOD/m<sup>2</sup> CCA in winter as compared to 0.049 (SE±0.03) in summer (Wilcoxon signed rank, n=14, p=0.88).

records.question: Which coral genus was found to be disproportionately affected by disease in Tutuila?
ground_truth_chunks: We found *Acropora* to be disproportionately affected by disease in Tutuila.

*Acropora* appear to be particularly susceptible to disease and this same pattern is emerging Indo-Pacific wide being found on the GBR (Willis et al. 2004), Sulawesi, Indonesia (Haapkyla et al. 2007) and the northwestern Hawaiian Islands (Aeby 2007).
